dedupe_keys.name: aeroscope open source global air traffic and co2 emission dataset

description: AeroSCOPE is a global open-source passenger air traffic dataset giving the seating capacity available on each origin-destination route in 2019, with the associated airline and aircraft type where known, for estimating commercial aviation CO2 emissions. Each row is an origin, destination, operator and aircraft type tuple with the airline IATA code, aircraft ICAO code and class, a proxy aircraft for performance modelling and the original source. It was built by aggregating open databases of limited coverage (such as Brazil's ANAC, Australian statistics, the US BTS T-100 and aggregated Eurocontrol data) and completing them with a route database parsed from Wikipedia and Wikidata, whose traffic was estimated with an XGBoost model. It was produced by Antoine Salgas, Junzi Sun, Scott Delbecq, Thomas Planès and Gilles Lafforgue. Coverage is global for 2019. Access: a free 67 MB CSV on Zenodo (version 1.0.1) under GPL-3.0-or-later; the authors ask to be contacted before commercial use. Caveats: route-level accuracy is limited, and the authors intend it for continental or country-level analyses. It supports air network flow modelling and aviation demand and emission scenarios, and complements the BTS T-100 statistics and the OpenSky Network catalogued here.
